keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the founding year: Cliopatria's first Natalia shape begins in 1840, but the page's infobox dates the republic's establishment to 12 October 1839. CORRECTED after the review of 2026-10-19: the shape is Cliopatria's 1840 shape minus Klip River county, the land north of the Tugela and west of the Buffalo. The page says 'Mpande gave up to Natal all the territory between the Buffalo and Tugela rivers, which later formed Klip River county' (in its narrative of the 1843 settlement, after the Natal Volksraad accepted Lord Stanley's terms on 8 August 1843; it dates the gift no closer) and 'Hitherto the Tugela River from source to mouth had been the recognized frontier between Natal and Zululand'. Cliopatria's 1840 shape holds 39 of its 141 cells (about 9,900 km2, Ladysmith and the Newcastle tip) north of the Tugela, which the colony received from Mpande in 1843 (colony-of-natal ledger), not the republic; the 10 Msinga cells that Cliopatria draws in Zululand were never in the republic's shape either. No infobox area on the page to compare (ratio not computable).

keyframe_review.note: Corrected shape as in natalia-republic_1839 (Cliopatria's 1840 shape minus Klip River county, about 25,800 km2): it serves the republic to the annexation of May 1843, after which colony-of-natal_1843 takes it and adds Klip River county and the Msinga cells. THE PROCLAIMED TRACT IS NOT DRAWN, AND WHY: on 29 January 1840 Dingane was crushed at Maqongqo; the Boers reached Mpande on 6 February 1840 and on 14 February 1840 Pretorius issued a proclamation that "a large stretch of land extending from St. Lucia Bay was now the border" between the Zulu kingdom and the Republic of Natalia (Battle of Maqongqe page, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Maqongqe; it gives no further boundary details). The Natalia page words it 'proclaimed a large tract of land extending from St Lucia Bay to be part of the Natalia Republic' (undated). Neither page gives an inland line, and the Natalia page has the Tugela as the 'recognized frontier' until Mpande's concession to Natal in 1843, so the proclamation is read as a claim, not as ground held, and Klip River county is left out. Alternative reading, for a later reviewer: if the proclamation is taken as putting the land north of the Tugela in the republic from 14 February 1840, Cliopatria's unchanged 1840 shape (37,668 km2, Klip River included) is the better one for 1840-1843, but the tract north of the Tugela toward St Lucia Bay would still be missing. Cliopatria's remaining Natalia shapes (1848-1910) are the British colony and are reviewed in colony-of-natal.

ledger.note: 12 October 1839: the Voortrekkers found the Republic of Natalia at Pietermaritzburg. Infobox Established: 12 October 1839 (the body gives no date); Retief and Dingane had signed the deed of cession on 4 February 1838 and the Boers defeated the Zulus at Blood River on 16 December 1838. The page gives no boundary for the grant, so the region is Cliopatria's Natal shape without Klip River county north of the Tugela, which the page says Mpande gave up to Natal only in 1843 (see natalia-republic_1839).

region.text: Port Natal (Durban), the harbour and settlement and the British camp at the Berea

ledger.note: 26 May 1842: the Boers take Port Natal from the British. 'On 23 May 1842, Smith's night attack on the Boer camp failed. On 26 May 1842, the Boers captured the harbour and settlement, and on 31 May they blockaded the British camp' (Captain T. C. Smith had reached Durban in April and camped at the Berea on 4 May).
26 June 1842: the British camp is relieved. Smith was relieved on 26 June 1842 (Dick King had ridden to Grahamstown, leaving on 24 May); Port Natal stays British and the Boers submit in 1843.

ledger.note: May 1843: Britain annexes Natalia. Infobox 'Annexed by Britain: 12 May 1843' (the Colony of Natal page proclaims the colony on 4 May 1843); the Natal Volksraad unanimously accepted the terms on 8 August 1843. Many Boers trekked over the Drakensberg into the Orange Free State and the Transvaal; about 500 families stayed. Klip River county north of the Tugela was not the republic's land to hand over: Mpande gave it to Natal in the settlement that followed the Volksraad's acceptance (colony-of-natal ledger).

wars.name: Boer-British conflict at Port Natal (Congella and the siege of the British camp)
wars.outcome: The Boers took the harbour on 26 May 1842 and blockaded the British camp; Smith was relieved on 26 June 1842; Britain annexed Natalia in May 1843.
wars.note: No separate article was opened (the Natalia page carries the dated sentences); Napier announced his intention to resume military occupation of Port Natal on 2 December 1841.

wars.name: Boer-Mpande campaign against Dingane (Battle of Maqongqo, First Zulu Civil War)
wars.outcome: Dingane was crushed at Maqongqo on 29 January 1840 (military phase from 14 January); the Boers arrived on 6 February, proclaimed Mpande king and returned to Natalia with 36,000 head of cattle; on 14 February 1840 Pretorius proclaimed that "a large stretch of land extending from St. Lucia Bay was now the border" with the Zulu kingdom. Dingane fled to Swaziland and was killed soon after (undated).
wars.note: Read from the Battle of Maqongqe page; the Natalia page (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natalia_Republic) has the alliance in the infobox as January 1840 and the proclaimed 'large tract of land extending from St Lucia Bay' (undated). The Maqongqe page dates the Boers' arrival to 6 February 1840, after the battle of 29 January. Neither page gives the tract's inland boundary, so no zone is drawn and the tract is not in any keyframe; the Zululand dossier (af-07-a) carries the Zulu side.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary for the republic: its south and west follow Cliopatria's Natal outline, the Tugela was the recognised frontier with Zululand until 1843 (the page), and the Drakensberg was set as the northern limit of Natal only in August 1843. Pretorius's St Lucia Bay claim (proclaimed 14 February 1840; Battle of Maqongqe page) has no inland line and is not drawn.

notes: One page opened for this republic (the colony years, 1843-1910, were read from the Colony of Natal page; see colony-of-natal; the combined budget for the two dossiers is five pages). SPLIT: Cliopatria's one row 'Natalia Republic' (1840-1910, 8 shapes, Wikipedia 'Natalia Republic', Q1029847) runs through the British Colony of Natal and the Natal Province's last years to 1910; the republic is 1839-1843 only. This dossier reviews the 1840 shape (and a new 1839 keyframe); the shapes 1848, 1856, 1877, 1885, 1898, 1900 and 1908 belong to colony-of-natal, so the validator warns that they have no verdict here (intended; they are reviewed there, and this dossier's cliopatria_names and the colony's are the same row). Colour: the republic is a Boer state (family africa) and Natal a British colony (family britain), so the two should take different colours; the colour agent should seed colony-of-natal. Not settled: (1) the republic's boundary; the page gives none. (2) The page's two annexation dates (infobox 12 May 1843; body 8 August 1843) and the Colony page's 4 May 1843; the ledger uses May. (3) Natal 'became part of Cape Colony in 1844 and was separated again in 1856' (Natalia page; the Colony page: 'administered from the Cape Colony in 1844', 'in 1856 the dependence of the country on Cape Colony was put to an end'); Cliopatria keeps Natal separate throughout. (4) Port Natal was annexed by the British on 4 December 1838 and their garrison withdrawn on 24 December 1839 (page), before the republic's founding. (5) The president is given as Andries Pretorius (1839-1843) on the infobox as relayed; no ruler strip is written because the page lists no succession. REPAIR 2026-10-19 (after review-af-07-b, verdict fail): (a) The first version drew the republic as Cliopatria's 1840 Natal shape unchanged, on the premise that the Buffalo-Tugela country was only the 10 Msinga cells Cliopatria draws in Zululand. The gazetteer shows otherwise: 39 of the shape's 141 cells (about 9,900 km2; Ladysmith, the Newcastle tip) lie north of the Tugela, i.e. in Klip River county, which the Natalia page says Mpande gave up to Natal and which it places in its 1843 settlement narrative after 8 August 1843 (undated beyond that); the page also says the Tugela from source to mouth had been the recognised frontier. Corrected: both keyframes, the found and dissolve events and the predecessor/successor land are Cliopatria's 1840 shape minus a box 28.8-30.7E, 27.4-28.75S (north of the Tugela). The reviewer's own test box started at 29.4E (34 cells); the box here runs west to 28.8E because the page puts the Tugela's whole course, source to mouth, on the frontier, which adds 5 cells along the upper river (the Drakensberg end, centres 28.5-28.7S). The region 'Klip River County' is not in the gazetteer: the polygon is the stand-in, to be replaced by the region once it exists. (b) The St Lucia Bay proclamation is now dated (14 February 1840, Battle of Maqongqe page: a large stretch of land extending from St. Lucia Bay 'was now the border') but not drawn: neither page gives an inland line and the Natalia page keeps the Tugela as the recognised frontier until 1843; the alternative reading (claim read as held land, so Klip River county stays in the republic) is written in the _1840 keyframe note. (c) Counterpart gaps for af-07-a: zululand has no 1843 loss of Klip River county and the Msinga cells to the colony, and its 1838 loss (Dingane's deed of 3-4 February 1838) is 20 months before the republic's 12 October 1839 founding, and the zululand keyframes need to hold Klip River county until 1843 now that the republic does not. The page was re-read; the Battle of Maqongqe page is a second page for this dossier (three pages in all with the Colony of Natal page, inside the pair's budget of five).
